video_title: Mike Conley Talks 20 Years in the NBA, Leadership & Life as a Veteran

quotes.speaker: Mike Conley
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Conley on the evolution of NBA sportsmanship awards
quotes.excerpt: Back then they were giving out big old glass trophies and it was a really nice
quotes.quote: It was probably my fifth or sixth year in the league, so it was probably 2012, 2013, somewhere around there. Back then they were giving out big old glass trophies and it was a really nice, and they've kind of gotten a little bit smaller, it's like the gold, I don't know if you get one yet, but it's like a little dude handshake, it's in there. It's like sitting right there.
quotes.social_post: Mike Conley reflects on the evolution of NBA sportsmanship awards, noting how the trophies have changed from big glass pieces to the current handshake design over his 20 year career.

quotes.speaker: Mike Conley
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Conley on the mutual respect between players and referees
quotes.excerpt: We have conversations. It's not like the respect. It's a mutual respect. They know not to call
quotes.quote: We have conversations. It's not like the respect. It's a mutual respect. They know not to call a tech on me. They know that for sure. It was Mani Mahloushi, I remember him forever, and he comes up to me anytime he sees me, he's like, 'Man, once again, I'm sorry about that. I didn't mean to, that was just frustrated and took it out on you,' but it got rescinded, so it doesn't count then.
quotes.social_post: Mike Conley says he has a mutual respect with NBA referees, joking that they know better than to call a technical foul on him.

quotes.speaker: Mike Conley
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Conley on his role as a pick-and-roll specialist
quotes.excerpt: I was always a big empty side pick and roll guy, so with it started many years back
quotes.quote: I was always a big empty side pick and roll guy, so with it started many years back with Marcus. Whatever big I had, they traveled to Rudy Gobert, and now here, and Minnesota, obviously Minnesota, but so we'd always find ways to get to it. It would be a call for most teams, but for me, it was like I just wave a guy out of the corner and just dribble as fast as I can in the corner and call for a pick and roll in the deep corner.
quotes.social_post: Mike Conley breaks down his signature pick and roll style, explaining how he developed the habit of waving teammates out of the corner to create space for himself.

quotes.speaker: Mike Conley
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Conley on his potential future as an NBA coach
quotes.excerpt: I'm not going to shut down the idea of being a coach. I don't necessarily want to be
quotes.quote: I'm not going to shut down the idea of being a coach. I don't necessarily want to be a coach. But I could, they have their opinions and I think they're rightfully so, they could be an ideal situation, but I'd rather be like management or like, you know, just be around the game, but I don't know if I can coach these young people. I don't know if I'm ready for it.
quotes.social_post: Mike Conley says he is not sure he is ready to coach young players in the NBA, noting he would prefer a role in management after he retires.

quotes.speaker: Mike Conley
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Conley's pre-game routine and dietary habits
quotes.excerpt: I've ate penne pasta before every game. I stopped eating red meat like 10 years ago
quotes.quote: I've ate penne pasta before every game. I stopped eating red meat like 10 years ago, so it used to be like a bolognese, like beef and stuff like that and I changed that to chicken, but that was like the only thing I did different as far as the pasta was concerned, but I do that every game day. The cold tubs and hot tubs are something I've done since I've been in the league, so it's just part of the routine.
quotes.social_post: Mike Conley shares his long standing game day routine, which includes eating penne pasta before every single game and avoiding red meat for the last decade.

quotes.speaker: Mike Conley
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Conley on the 'Good Guys Finish First' brand philosophy
quotes.excerpt: The idea behind it was just basically that there is this avenue where good guys can accomplish
quotes.quote: The idea behind it was just basically that there is this avenue where good guys can accomplish a lot of great things. You don't have to be the meanest person or stepping over people and always clearing a path. And just this idea that was brought to a lot of people that you have to be a certain way in order to be successful. I didn't agree with that, and I think that you should find that power within all the people who try to do things the right way and raise a certain way and maybe a little bit quieter or shy or whatever you may be, but you still have the same chances of success as anybody else.
quotes.social_post: Mike Conley discusses his philosophy that good guys can finish first, arguing that you do not have to be mean or aggressive to find success in the NBA.

quotes.excerpt: I think he got a very unpredictable side of the trade

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Conley
text_blocks.text: I think you are doing a great job as the commissioner. Very pointed advice because he benefited from his philosophy.

text_blocks.speaker: Josh Jacobs
text_blocks.text: I think he got a very unpredictable side of the trade. Where Josh Jacobs, yes, is a great player, but I don't know what his status is going forward. I don't know if something happens.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Conley
text_blocks.text: That is a little bit of a risk.

text_blocks.speaker: Josh Jacobs
text_blocks.text: Malik Neighbors, great talent, great player, he is coming back from injury. There is a lot of gray area, but Bijan Robinson is Bijan Robinson. We know that. It is like you know what you are going to get.

quotes.social_post: A discussion on fantasy football trade risks, evaluating the status of Josh Jacobs and Malik Neighbors compared to the consistency of Bijan Robinson.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Conley
text_blocks.text: Give me Kyren. Kyren for Trey McBride.

text_blocks.speaker: Josh Jacobs
text_blocks.text: I could do the same thing, give you Kyren for Malik Neighbors and Josh Jacobs.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Conley
text_blocks.text: He is not -- no, no, no. We are not doing that.

quotes.social_post: The group debates a potential trade involving Kyren Williams and Trey McBride, with a firm refusal to move forward with the proposed deal.

quotes.speaker: Trey McBride
quotes.summary_phrase: Trey McBride's consistent performance and value
quotes.excerpt: Trey McBride is solid. He is a Colorado kid.
quotes.quote: Trey McBride is solid. He is a Colorado kid. He is the goat. He shows up every week. He is good for like 14 points.
quotes.social_post: Trey McBride is described as a solid and consistent performer who shows up every week to deliver production.
